title: Provable State Estimation with Recurrent Models
claim: A contracting recurrent observer maps observations to a latent state whose trajectories forget initial conditions and converge to the true quantity.
layout: 2 panels: vertical block pipeline left, convergence curve plots right, math throughout
description: The left panel is a vertical stack of three rounded, color-coded boxes joined by downward arrows. A blue Physical System box holds the equations x-dot = f(x), o = h(x), s = σ(x). An orange Contracting RNN box holds z-dot = κ g_Ω(z, o). A green MLP Decoder box holds ŝ = γ_Ω(z). Arrows are labeled o(t) and z(t). A dashed blue loop labeled T_κ embedding sits beside the first arrow. At the bottom, ŝ(t) → s(t) as t→∞. The right panel is titled 'Contracting property'. It has two stacked boxes, an orange one for latent space Z and a green one for output space S. Each box shows red, blue, purple and green curves converging to a common line. Inequality callouts state exponential contraction and an ε-bound on the estimation error.
caption: Provable state estimation: a contracting Neural ODE with latent dynamics ˙z = κgΩ(z, o) processes observations o(t) from the physical system with unobserved x(t), of which elements s(t) are of interest. A decoder γΩmaps the latent state to an estimate ˆs(t). The existence of an injective state-to-latent map Tκ : X →Z is guaranteed (Theorems 3.4-3.7). A contraction property ensures that two latent trajectories za, zb initialized anywhere in Z exponentially forgets initial conditions. The estimate ˆs(t) reaches an ϵ-neighborhood of the true s(t) after a finite observation time, and increasing κ accelerates convergence at the cost of larger network capacity (Theorem 4.2).
abstract: Estimating the state of a dynamical system from observations is a crucial task in robotics and control. Despite their empirical success, recurrent models often lack formal guarantees on convergence and robustness. We bridge this gap by analyzing these architectures from the perspective of nonlinear observer theory. By framing RNNs as a time-discretization of continuous latent dynamical systems (Neural ODEs), we demonstrate that enforcing a contraction condition on the latent flow guarantees the existence of a smooth, injective map of the true physical state into the latent space. We prove that this architecture acts as a tunable observer: by increasing a single scalar gain that scales the latent vector field, the estimation error can be driven to an arbitrarily small neighborhood of zero at an exponentially fast rate. We further establish quantitative bounds on the MLP complexity required to decode this latent state, and extend our formal guarantees to the discrete-time residual RNN implementation. We validate the theory on a real mobile robotic task, where a provably contracting model outperforms a vanilla GRU with substantially more stable training. We also report that unconstrained GRUs converge to contracting dynamics on this task, suggesting that contraction is an emergent property of well-trained sequence models.
